ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r4.claim: The Day will be cataclysmic for people dreaming of worldly luxuries: those who arrogantly refuse prostration now will then be called to bow but unable.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p438/r4.anchor: whilst these people may be dreaming of having the same luxuries they have here, that Day will be very cataclysmic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r1.claim: On Judgment Day their backs will be too rigid to prostrate even if they wish; downcast eyes and encompassing ignominy will display their helplessness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r1.anchor: in spite of wanting to prostrate, they will not be able to do so

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r2.claim: The call to prostrate humiliates them and shows their denial had no excuse, with their own beings testifying to arrogance and deprivation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r2.anchor: their own being will bear irrefutable testimony to their arrogance and deprivation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p439/r3.claim: Al-Maʿārij 70:43–44 parallels the scene; its emergence from graves with downcast eyes and ignominy clarifies that ‘the Day the shin is exposed’ means a day of severe upheaval.

QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r15.claim: The warning may confront people at the end of worldly life or at the beginning of the next; recalling their earlier call to prostrate intensifies regret and makes the proof decisive.
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r15.anchor: يذكرهم بذلك ليزدادوا حسرة ، ولتكون الحجة عليهم أبلغ

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r4.claim: At the call, God removes their ability to prostrate and blocks their capacity, heightening regret for neglecting the call when their limbs were sound.

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r7.claim: Khāshiʿatan absāruhum is a circumstantial phrase linked to their inability to prostrate.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r7.anchor: أما قوله : { خاشعة أبصارهم } فهو حال

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r8.claim: Their eyes are downcast and humiliation overtakes them because they did not persist in serving their master, like a servant abandoned by his master and shamed among people.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r8.anchor: يعني يلحقهم ذل بسبب أنهم ما كانوا مواظبين على خدمة مولاهم مثل العبد الذي أعرض عنه مولاه

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r9.claim: In worldly life they were called to prayer by the adhān and iqāma while healthy and able to pray.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r9.anchor: يعني حين كانوا يدعون إلى الصلوات بالأذان والإقامة وكانوا سالمين قادرين على الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r10.claim: The passage threatens those who stay away from congregational prayer and do not answer the muezzin’s call to join it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p84/r10.anchor: وفي هذا وعيد لمن قعد عن الجماعة ولم يجب المؤذن إلى إقامة الصلاة في الجماعة

STUDYQURAN:68:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r1.claim: Although some Arabs considered the bodily position of prostration humiliating, the disbelievers will face greater humiliation in the Hereafter and be unable to prostrate.
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r1.anchor: but in the Hereafter the disbelievers will find much greater humiliation and be unable to prostrate, as mentioned in v. 42

STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the prostration in both verses as prostration for prayer in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:68:43/r2.anchor: references to prostrating for prayer in this world

TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.claim: Abdullah reports that people are questioned about whom they worship; when the shank is disclosed, believers prostrate while hypocrites' backs become flat and rigid.
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: يتمثل الله للخلق يوم القيامة حتى يمر المسلمون، قال: فيقول: من تعبدون؟

TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud describes forty years of standing, idol worshippers being led to Hell, and believers prostrating while hypocrites cannot; believers then enter Paradise and receive its rewards.
TAB-FULL:v23p189/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: ينادي مناد يوم القيامة: أليس عدلا من ربكم الذي خلقكم

TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.claim: Abdullah tells Umar that after forty years of standing, each people follows its objects of worship to Hell; Muslims prostrate when the Lord appears, but hypocrites cannot and are sent to Hell, while believers enter Paradise and are rewarded.
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r1.anchor: عن قيس بن سكن، قال: حدث عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.claim: A second account from Abdullah to Umar repeats the gathering, idol-following and return to God, where true worshippers prostrate and hypocrites' backs stiffen before they are taken to Hell.
TAB-FULL:v23p191/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله وهو يحدث عمر

TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report: worshippers prostrate at the disclosure, hypocrites' backs fuse, and survivors cross the bridge at different speeds according to their light; al-Tabari abridges a longer report.
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " حتى إن أحدهم ليلتف فيكشف عن ساق، فيقعون سجودا

TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that idol worshippers, Jews and Christians follow what they worship to Hell; those left recognize God at the disclosure and prostrate, while hypocrites who did not prostrate sincerely cannot.
TAB-FULL:v23p194/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى مناد: ألا لتلحق كل أمة بما كانت تعبد

TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.claim: A second transmission from Abu Sa'id repeats that each group follows what it worshipped; the remaining people wait for their Lord, whose coming is related to the preceding account.
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ينادي مناديه فيقول: ليلحق كل قوم بما كانوا يعبدون

TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that after settling wrongs, God sends angels resembling Uzayr and Jesus and presents false gods; believers affirm only God, recognize Him by a sign and prostrate, while hypocrites fall backward with rigid spines.
TAB-FULL:v23p195/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " يأخذ الله للمظلوم من الظالم حتى إذا لم يبق تبعة لأحد عند أحد

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r1.claim: The humbled eyes are overwhelmed by humiliation from God's punishment.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r1.anchor: فيقسو ظهر المنافق عن السجود، ويجعل الله سجود المؤمنين عليهم توبيخا وذلا وصغارا، وندامة وحسرة

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r2.claim: They had been called to prostrate to God in worldly life while safe, with no impediment keeping them from doing so.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r2.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون}

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the prostration means the prescribed prayer.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي، {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون} [القلم: 43] قال: إلى الصلاة المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains it as hearing the caller to the prescribed prayer but not answering.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود} [القلم: 43] قال: يسمع المنادي إلى الصلاة المكتوبة فلا يجيبه

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the disbelievers were called to prostrate safely in worldly life, whereas now they are summoned in fear.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون} [القلم: 43] قال: هم الكفار كانوا يدعون في الدنيا وهم آمنون

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari links the polytheists' inability to obey in this life and the next: 11:20 says they could not hear or see, and here they cannot prostrate with humbled eyes.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r6.anchor: فإنه قال {ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون} [هود: 20] وأما في الآخرة فإنه قال: {فلا يستطيعون خاشعة أبصارهم} [القلم: 43]

TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.claim: Qatada transmits a Prophetic report that believers will be allowed to prostrate at the Resurrection; hypocrites cannot, and believers' prostration rebukes and humiliates them.
TAB-FULL:v23p196#2/r7.anchor: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: «يؤذن للمؤمنين يوم القيامة في السجود، فيسجد المؤمنون

TAB-FULL:v23p198/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p198/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p198/r1.claim: Al-Tabari clarifies that both the summons to prostrate and their being safe refer to worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v23p198/r1.anchor: أي في الدنيا {وهم سالمون} [القلم: 43] أي في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v23p198/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p198/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p198/r2.claim: Qatada says believers will be permitted to prostrate at the Resurrection between believers and hypocrites; believers prostrate, hypocrites cannot, and the prostration reproaches them.
TAB-FULL:v23p198/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قال: بلغني أنه يؤذن للمؤمنين يوم القيامة في السجود بين كل مؤمنين منافق، يسجد المؤمنون، ولا يستطيع المنافق أن يسجد

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.claim: These five verses interrupt the discussion because the alleged partners were supposed to secure happiness after resurrection; there are no partners or intercession, and afterlife felicity comes from worldly submission to God’s unity in lordship.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r4.anchor: والآية وما بعدها إلى تمام خمس آيات اعتراض وقع في البين بمناسبة ذكر شركائهم الذين يزعمون أنهم سيسعدونهم لو كان هناك بعث وحساب

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r6.claim: “Their eyes humbled” and “humiliation overwhelms them” are two circumstantial clauses describing those summoned; humility is assigned to the eyes because its effects appear there.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r6.anchor: حالان من نائب فاعل يدعون أي حال كون أبصارهم خاشعة وحال كونهم يغشاهم الذلة

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r8.claim: One explanation of “safe” is that they were free in worldly life from the afflictions that later deprived their souls of the capacity to answer truth.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r8.anchor: المراد بالسلامة سلامتهم من الآفات والعاهات التي لحقت نفوسهم بسبب الاستكبار عن الحق

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, “safe” means simply that they had the ability to prostrate in worldly life.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r9.anchor: أو المراد مطلق استطاعتهم منه في الدنيا

TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r10.claim: The proposed interpretation that prostration means ritual prayer is dismissed by the author.
TABATABAI:68:34-52#2/r10.anchor: وقيل المراد بالسجود الصلاة وهو كما ترى

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r2.claim: Khāshiʿatan is a circumstantial accusative connected with those summoned, and their eyes are its grammatical subject.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r2.anchor: حال من مروفع يدعون على أن أبصارهم مرتفع به على الفاعلية

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r3.claim: Humility is attributed to the eyes because its effects show there, although all limbs are humbled and the heart is the true source of humility.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r3.anchor: ونسبة الخشوع إلى الأبصار لظهور أثره فيها وإلا فالأعضاء أيضا خاشعة ذليلة

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r4.speaker: الكشافي
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r4.claim: Al-Kāshifī glosses the description as people with lowered eyes, heads bowed and ashamed.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r4.anchor: يعني خداوندان أبصار سر دريش افكنده

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r5.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r5.claim: Abū al-Layth says Muslims' faces become white as snow after prostration, while Jews, Christians, and hypocrites who could not prostrate grieve and have blackened faces.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو الليث وذلك إن المسلمين إذا رفعوا رؤوسهم من السجود

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r6.claim: Tarhaquhum means that disgrace reaches and envelops them; rahq denotes one thing covering another.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r6.anchor: تلحقهم وتغشاهم فإن الرهق غشيان الشيء الشيء

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r7.claim: Dhilla is severe humiliating disgrace, glossed by the root's forms for abasement and the adjective dhalīl, humiliated.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r7.anchor: شديدة تخزيهم كأنه تفسير لخشوع أبصارهم يقال ذل يذل

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r8.claim: In worldly life they had been summoned by an obligatory call to prostrate; explicit wording replaces a pronoun for emphasis, or because prostration stands for prayer and its prostrations.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r8.anchor: لزيادة التقرير أولأن المراد به الصلاة أو ما فيها من السجود

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r9.claim: Prostration is singled out because it is the greatest act of obedience.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r9.anchor: وخص السجود بالذكر من حيث إنه أعظم الطاعات

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r10.claim: Some say the summons came through God's call, implicitly in the command to establish prayer or explicitly through the Prophet's call; one Prophetic report says a servant is closest to the Lord while prostrating and should supplicate much.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r10.anchor: قال بعضهم يدعون بدعوة الله ريحا مثل قوله تعالى : [القلم : 43]{واسجدوا واعبدوا}

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r11.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r11.claim: The Prophet's instruction to pray the five prayers, fast the month, give zakat, and obey the commands promised entry into the Lord's Paradise is presented as an implicit invitation to prostrate.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r11.anchor: كقوله علي السلام صلوا خمسكم وصوموا شهركم

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r12.claim: Scholars in every age also invite people to prostrate; the call of the adhān and iqāma, especially ḥayya ʿalā al-ṣalāh, is unmistakable, and answering willingly brings felicity.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r12.anchor: فإن قولهم حي على الصلاة دعوة بلا مرية فطوبى لمن أجاب دعوتهم بطوع لا بإكراه

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r13.claim: The clause wa-hum sālimūn is circumstantial, describing those summoned in worldly life.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r13.anchor: حال من ضمير يدعون وهم سالمون} حال من مرفوع يدعون الثاني

BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r14.claim: They were healthy, with sound limbs and joints and fully able to prostrate and answer the call; they rejected it then and now have only regret.
BURSEVI:v10p93#2/r14.anchor: أي أصحاء في الدنيا سلمت أعضاؤهم ومفاصلهم من الآفات والعلل

TABRISI:68:42-45/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:42-45/r4.claim: Their eyes are lowered in humiliation and they do not lift their gaze from the ground.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r4.anchor: أي ذليلة أبصارهم لا يرفعون نظرهم عن الأرض ذلة ومهانة

TABRISI:68:42-45/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:42-45/r5.claim: The disgrace of regret and grief overwhelms them.

TABRISI:68:42-45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:42-45/r6.claim: In worldly life they were healthy and able to prostrate, and were commanded to pray but did not.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r6.anchor: أي أصحاء يمكنهم السجود فلا يسجدون يعني أنهم كانوا يؤمرون بالصلاة في الدنيا

TABRISI:68:42-45/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:68:42-45/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they heard the call 'Come to success' but did not answer it.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r7.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير كانوا يسمعون حي على الفلاح فلا يجيبون

TABRISI:68:42-45/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r8.speaker: كعب الأحبار
TABRISI:68:42-45/r8.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar swore that the verse concerns people who fail to attend congregational prayers.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r8.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا في الذين يتخلفون عن الجماعات

TABRISI:68:42-45/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r9.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
TABRISI:68:42-45/r9.claim: Although paralyzed and carried between two men to the mosque, al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym refused an offered concession, saying whoever hears 'Come to success' must answer even by crawling.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r9.anchor: أنه عرض له الفالج فكان يهادى بين رجلين إلى المسجد فقيل له: يا أبا يزيد لو جلست

TABRISI:68:42-45/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:68:42-45/r10.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abdullah describe them struck with awe, fixed stares, hearts at their throats, and regret; in life they could obey commands and avoid prohibitions.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r10.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله ع أنهما قالا في هذه الآية أفحم القوم ودخلتهم الهيبة

TABRISI:68:42-45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:42-45/r11.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:68:42-45/r11.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say a caller summons people to prostrate on Resurrection Day; believers prostrate while hypocrites' backs stiffen, making Muslims' prostration a source of hypocrites' regret.
TABRISI:68:42-45/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة يؤذن المؤذن يوم القيامة فيسجد المؤمن وتصلب ظهور المنافقين

THALABI:v10p19/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p19/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p19/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the comparison of seeing God to the unobscured sun and full moon; at judgment false gods lead their worshippers away, while remaining believers recognize God at the sign of the shin and prostrate, unlike hypocrites.
THALABI:v10p19/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله هل نرى ربنا يوم القيامة؟

THALABI:v10p21/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v10p21/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports that nations follow their objects of worship toward the Fire; the remaining worshippers of God reject a false claim, recognize God when the shin is uncovered, and prostrate, while hypocrites cannot.
THALABI:v10p21/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى مناد

THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.claim: A report transmitted by al-Tabari from Abdullah, who was with Umar, says people stand barefoot and naked for forty years; at the divine sign true worshippers prostrate, hypocrites cannot, and the former enter Paradise while the latter enter the Fire.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r1.anchor: عن المنهال عن قيس بن بكر، قال: حدثني عبد الله وهو عند عمر قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة

THALABI:v10p21#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p21#2/r2.claim: The verse describes hypocrites unable to prostrate; believers raise bright faces, while disbelievers and hypocrites' faces darken.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أن المؤمنين يرفعون رؤوسهم ووجوههم أشد بياضا من الثلج، وتسود وجوه الكافرين والمنافقين.

THALABI:v10p21#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p21#2/r3.claim: They had been called to prostrate in worldly life while healthy and able, but refused.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r3.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون في الدنيا. إلى السجود وهم سالمون أصحاء فلا يأتونه ويأبونه.

THALABI:v10p21#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
THALABI:v10p21#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the call was to the obligatory prayer through the call to prayer and its commencement.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r4.anchor: قال إبراهيم التيمي: يدعون إلى الصلاة المكتوبة بالأذان والإقامة فيأبونه.

THALABI:v10p21#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p21#2/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they heard the call to success but did not come.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا يسمعون حي على الفلاح فلا يجيئون.

THALABI:v10p21#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p21#2/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v10p21#2/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says the verse was revealed only about people who stay away from congregational prayers.
THALABI:v10p21#2/r6.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا في الذين يتخلفون عن الجماعات.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r1.claim: Their eyes are humbled when they become certain of the punishment and see the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: يعني حين أيقنوا بالعذاب وعاينوا النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r2.claim: The phrase describing their eyes is a circumstantial clause attached to “they cannot.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r2.anchor: وهي حال من قوله: {فلا يستطيعون}. {ترهقهم ذلة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r3.claim: The humiliation that overtakes them is the disgrace of regret and remorse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يلحقهم ذل الندامة والحسرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r4.claim: In worldly life they were called and commanded to perform the obligatory prayer while healthy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r4.anchor: قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون} يعني في الدنيا حين كانوا يدعون إلى الصلاة المكتوبة ويؤمرون بها وهم معافون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل وإبراهيم التيمي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r5.claim: They understood the call to prayer as the adhan and iqama.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r5.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {يدعون} أي بالأذان والإقامة. وهذا الذي ذكرنا قول ابن عباس ومقاتل وإبراهيم التيمي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r6.claim: They heard the call “Come to success” but did not answer it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r6.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا يسمعون حي على الفلاح فلا يجيبون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r7.claim: The verse warns those who miss congregational prayer and do not answer the call to join it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p117/r7.anchor: وفي هذا وعيد لمن قعد عن الجماعة ولم يجب الأذان إلى إقامة الصلاة في الجماعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r1.claim: Their eyes are humbled and do not lift; humiliation overwhelms them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r1.anchor: { خاشعة أبصارهم } ذليلة لا يرفعونها { ترهقهم } تغشاهم { ذلة وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r2.claim: In worldly life they were called to prostrate while healthy but refused to worship God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:43-44/r2.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود } في الدنيا { وهم سالمون } فيأبون ولا يسجدون لله.

QASHANI:68:43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:43/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:43/r1.claim: Their eyes are humbled and confused because their luminous faculty is gone, leaving them unable to gaze at the world of light or perceive its joyful radiance.
QASHANI:68:43/r1.anchor: ذليلة متحيرة لذهاب قوتها النورية وعدم قدرتها على النظر إلى عالم النور

QASHANI:68:43/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:43/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:43/r2.claim: Humiliation is their attachment to lower things, stagnation in inferior passive states, and persistence in bodily nature.
QASHANI:68:43/r2.anchor: الركون إلى السفليات والركود إلى خساسة الانفعاليات وملازمة الطبيعيات

QASHANI:68:43/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:43/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:43/r3.claim: They had been called to surrender and prepare to receive the influx of the world of light while their faculties and readiness remained.

QASHANI:68:43/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:43/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:43/r4.claim: They were then sound in their capacity and able to attain happiness in the next life.
QASHANI:68:43/r4.anchor: الاستعداد متمكنون على إحراز السعادة في المعاد

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet: after each person is sent to follow the worldly deity they worshipped, Muslims recognize their Lord by the unveiling of the shin and prostrate, while hypocrites cannot bend their backs.
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r6.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan, Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den bir hadis rivayet etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:68:40-50/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r7.speaker: Dârekutnî ve Hâkim
ELMALILI:68:40-50/r7.claim: Al-Daraqutni and al-Hakim grade the Ibn Mas'ud narration sound.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.claim: Abu Muslim proposes either a person's last day, when angels appear without glad tidings and a late conversion no longer helps, or an illness, old age, or incapacity that prevents prostration despite earlier soundness.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r6.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kavlidir ki bugün kıyamet günü değil, dünyadadır

ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.claim: Elmalılı allows Abu Muslim's worldly reading but rejects his claim that Resurrection is impossible: the call there is reproach and condemnation, not a legal command; their imposed inability increases regret for neglecting prostration while sound.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#2/r7.anchor: âyetin lafzını Ebû Müslim’in dediğine haml mümkin

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.claim: The terrifying force of the disclosure is painful humiliation and crushing dread for criminals, but an enticing joy and honor for Muslims.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r11.anchor: mücrimlere mahz-ı elem olan hevl-engiz bir kahr u tezlil, müslimlere de aynı hâile içinde murad kapısını açan câzibeli bir şevk ve izzet heyecânı

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r15.claim: Their eyes are humbled and they are so abased that they cannot even gesture; humiliation keeps engulfing them.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r15.anchor: kendilerini bir zillet saracak da saracak

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r16.claim: In worldly life they were safely and freely invited to prostrate and obey, but rejected the invitation and failed to value its reward or their safety.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r16.anchor: Hâlbuki vaktiyle dünyada başları selâmette iken o secdeye davet olunuyorlardı tav‘an secde ve inkıyad etmeleri kendilerine teklif olunuyordu da onu reddediyorlardı.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r17.claim: They thought sinners were wiser than believers; now they will long to perform the very prostration they once refused, but will be powerless and defeated.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#3/r17.anchor: O selâmetin kadrini bilmiyorlar, rızâ ve ihtiyarlarıyla secdeye yanaşmıyorlar, itaatin sevâbına âkıbette zevkine inanmıyorlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.claim: Razi says unbelievers will be summoned to prostrate as a means of reproach and rebuke because they did not prostrate in worldly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r5.anchor: Râzî’ye göre inkârcılar dünyada Allah’a secde etmedikleri için âhirette kınanmak ve azarlanmak maksadıyla secdeye çağrılacaklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.claim: A hadith says men and women prostrate; those who prostrated ostentatiously in life will wish to prostrate then but will be unable to bend.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r6.anchor: Hadiste buyurulduğu üzere erkek kadın herkes Allah’a secde eder; dünyada gösteriş için secde etmiş olanlar da secde etmek isterler, fakat eğilemezler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.claim: A further narration says that even unbelievers will wish to prostrate but will lack the ability to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r7.anchor: inkârcıların da secde etmek isteyecekleri fakat buna güçlerinin yetmeyeceği haber verilmiştir (Şevkânî, V, 317)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r8.claim: They will be fearful-eyed, humiliated, and in a wretched state; since they refused when able to prostrate in life, their ability to do so will be taken away in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:42/r8.anchor: Halbuki dünyada yapabilecek durumda iken de secdeye çağrılmışlar, fakat secde etmemişlerdi. Bu sebeple âhirette secde etme güçleri ellerinden alınacaktır

BURHAN:v2p103/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r1.claim: Three excellences may occur separately across kinds of speech, but their combination in one kind occurs only in God's speech, whose knowledge encompasses everything.
BURHAN:v2p103/r1.anchor: وقد توجد هذه الفضائل الثلاث على التفرق فى أنواع الكلام وأما أن توجد مجمة عى فى نوع واحد منه فلم توجد إلا فى كلام العليم القدير

BURHAN:v2p103/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r2.claim: The Qur'an is inimitable through the most eloquent words, finest composition, soundest meanings, and exact placement of every element.
BURHAN:v2p103/r2.anchor: فخرج من هذا أن القرآن إنما صار معجزا لأنه جاء بأفصح الألفاظ فى أحسن نظوم التأليف مضمنا أصح المعانى

BURHAN:v2p103/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r3.claim: Its sound meanings include God's oneness and transcendence, worship and its laws, exhortation, moral correction, right conduct, and warning against vice.
BURHAN:v2p103/r3.anchor: من توحيد الله تعالى وتنزيهه فى صفاته ودعاء إلى طاعته وبيان لطريق عبادته فى تحليل وتحريم وحظر وإباحة ومن وعظ وتقويم

BURHAN:v2p103/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r4.claim: The Qur'an joins accounts of past peoples and their punishments with reports of future events, combining proof with what it proves to reinforce its commands.
BURHAN:v2p103/r4.anchor: مودعا أخبار القرون الماضية وما نزل من مثلات الله بمن عصى وعاند منهم منبئا عن الكوائن المستقبلة فى الأعصار الماضية من الزمان

BURHAN:v2p103/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r5.claim: Humans cannot produce an equivalent work or match its form, because they cannot unite these diverse elements into an ordered whole.
BURHAN:v2p103/r5.anchor: ومعلوم أن الإتيان بمثل هذه الأمور والجمع بين أشتاتها حتى تنتظم وتتسق أمر تعجز عنه قوى البشر ولا تبلغه قدرتهم

BURHAN:v2p103/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r6.claim: Opponents called it poetry because it was composed and magic because they could not match it, while admitting its sweetness and powerful effect on the heart.
BURHAN:v2p103/r6.anchor: يقولون مرة إنه شعر لما رأوه منظوما ومرة إنه سحرلما رأوه معجوزا عنه غير مقدور عليه

BURHAN:v2p103/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p103/r7.claim: Some opponents called the Qur'an legends written and dictated to Muhammad, despite knowing he was unlettered and had no nearby person to dictate or write for him.
BURHAN:v2p103/r7.anchor: مع علمهم أن صاحبهم أمى وليس بحضرته من يملى أو يكتب شيئا

BURHAN:v2p103/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p103/r8.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي
BURHAN:v2p103/r8.claim: After prolonged, frustrated reflection on the Qur'an, al-Walīd could say only that it was human speech, out of stubbornness and inability to answer its proof.
BURHAN:v2p103/r8.anchor: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومى أنه لما طال فكره فى القآن وكثر ضجره منه

ITQAN:v4p320/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r1.claim: The Qur’an excels in eloquent, weighty, sweet wording, harmonious arrangement, and meanings of the highest rank.
ITQAN:v4p320/r1.anchor: وجدت هذه الأمور منه في غاية الشرف والفضيلة حتى لا ترى شيئا من الألفاظ أفصح ولا أجزل ولا أعذب من ألفاظه

ITQAN:v4p320/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r2.claim: These three excellences occur separately in other speech, but only God’s speech combines them together.
ITQAN:v4p320/r2.anchor: أن توجد مجموعة في نوع واحد منه فلم توجد إلا في كلام العليم القدير

ITQAN:v4p320/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability combines eloquent form with sound doctrine, worship, law, moral exhortation, and ethical guidance.
ITQAN:v4p320/r3.anchor: إنما صار معجزا لأنه جاء بأفصح الألفاظ في أحسن نظوم التأليف مضمنا أصح المعاني من توحيد لله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p320/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r4.claim: It unites proof with what is proved and evidence with its conclusion, reinforcing its invitation and commands.
ITQAN:v4p320/r4.anchor: جامعا في ذلك بين الحجة والمحتج له والدليل والمدلول عليه ليكون ذلك آكد للزوم ما دعا عليه

ITQAN:v4p320/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r5.claim: The ordered combination of diverse qualities exceeds human power, leaving people unable to match or counter the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v4p320/r5.anchor: تعجز عنه قوى البشر ولا تبلغه قدرتهم فانقطع الخلق دونه وعجزوا عن معارضته بمثله أو مناقضته في شكله

ITQAN:v4p320/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r6.claim: Opponents called it poetry for its form and sorcery because they could not match it, yet acknowledged its sweetness and beauty; others called it ancient fables.
ITQAN:v4p320/r6.anchor: يقولون مرة إنه شعر لما رأوه منظوما ومرة أنه سحر لما رأوه معجوزا عنه غير مقدور عليه

ITQAN:v4p320/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p320/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p320/r7.claim: The charge that it was dictated lore conflicted with their knowledge that Muhammad was unlettered and had no one present to dictate or write.
ITQAN:v4p320/r7.anchor: ﴿ أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا ﴾ مع علمهم أن صاحبهم أمي وليس بحضرته من يملي أو يكتب

KHATTABI:v1p28/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r1.claim: The Qurʾān’s coordination of diverse elements into a coherent whole exceeds human capacity, leaving people unable to produce a comparable work or counter-form.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r1.anchor: ومعلوم أن الإتيان بمثل هذه الأمور , والجمع بين شتاتها حتى تنتظم وتتسق أمر تعجز عنه قوى البشر

KHATTABI:v1p28/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r2.claim: Opponents alternately called the Qurʾān poetry because it is ordered and sorcery because they could not match it; its sweetness and effect on hearts unsettled them.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r2.anchor: يقولون مرة إنه شعر لما رأوه كلاما منظوما , ومرة سحر إذ رأوه معجوزا عنه

KHATTABI:v1p28/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r3.claim: The author tentatively identifies the man who deliberated over the Qurʾān as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; the Qurʾān recounts his reflection and his claim that it was human speech and sorcery.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r3.anchor: ويقال هو الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

KHATTABI:v1p28/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r4.claim: The central principle of eloquence is placing each kind of word in its most fitting position; substitution either corrupts meaning or removes stylistic brilliance.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r4.anchor: عمود هذه البلاغة التي تجمع لها هذه الصفات هو وضع كل نوع من الألفاظ التي تشتمل عليها فصول الكلام موضعه

KHATTABI:v1p28/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r5.claim: Words often mistaken for synonyms—such as knowledge and recognition, praise and gratitude, or stinginess and miserliness—retain distinguishing nuances despite partial overlap.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r5.anchor: لأن كل لفظة منها خاصية تتميز بها عن صاحبتها في بعض معانيها وإن كانا قد يشتركان في بعضها

KHATTABI:v1p28/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r6.claim: Maʿrifa takes one object, as in knowing Zayd, whereas ʿilm takes two, as in knowing Zayd to be intelligent.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r6.anchor: وعلمت يقتضي مفعولين , كقولك: علمت زيدا عاقلا

KHATTABI:v1p28/r7.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p28/r7.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p28/r7.claim: The author says one says ‘I recognize God’ but not ‘I know God’ without an accompanying attribute, such as knowing Him to be just or powerful.
KHATTABI:v1p28/r7.anchor: فتقول عرفت الله , ولا تقول علمت الله , إلا أن تضيف إليه صفة من الصفات

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p481#2/r1.claim: The humiliation covers or overwhelms them.

MAJAZ:v2p266/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p266/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p266/r1.claim: Tarhaquhum means it covers or overtakes them.

NAHHAS:v5p14/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r11.claim: خاشعة is circumstantial accusative and أبصارهم its nominative agent; alternatively both words are nominative as subject and predicate.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r11.anchor: نصب على الحال ( أبصارهم ) رفع بالخشوع ويجوز رفعهما جميعا على المبتدأ

NAHHAS:v5p14/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r12.claim: ترهقهم ذلة can be an accusative circumstantial clause or detached from the preceding one.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r12.anchor: ( ترهقهم ذلة ) في موضع نصب أيضا على الحال ويجوز قطعه من الأول

NAHHAS:v5p14/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p14/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p14/r13.claim: They had been called to prostration while safe in worldly life.
NAHHAS:v5p14/r13.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون ) أي في الدنيا

SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r1.claim: خاشعة is circumstantial from the subject of يدعون, while أبصارهم is its grammatical subject.
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r1.anchor: قوله: { خاشعة }: حال من مرفوع " يدعون " و " أبصارهم " فاعل به

SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r2.claim: Humility is attributed to the eyes though all the limbs are humble, because its visible effect appears in the eyes.
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r2.anchor: ونسب الخشوع للأبصار، وإن كانت الأعضاء كلها كذلك لظهور أثره فيها

SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r3.claim: وهم سالمون is circumstantial, with its subject the subject of the second يدعون.
SAMIN-DURR:68:43/r3.anchor: وقوله: { وهم سالمون } حال من مرفوع " يدعون " الثانية

ZAJJAJ:v5p211/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p211/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p211/r2.claim: They were called to prostrate while they were still sound and safe in worldly life.
ZAJJAJ:v5p211/r2.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون (43) يعني به في الدنيا

NASHR:v2p194#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p194#2/r1.claim: Earlier reading authorities generally did not discuss combining readings in one completion; al-Ṣafrawī briefly hints at it without substance. The author calls the topic useful and the fruit of the book's preceding principles.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r1.anchor: لم يتعرض أحد من أئمة القراءة في تواليفهم لهذا الباب. وقد أشار إليه أبو القاسم الصفراوي في إعلانه، ولم يأت بطائل

NASHR:v2p194#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p194#2/r2.claim: The author attributes the omission to early readers' zeal for comprehensive study: they repeated a single transmission through several full readings with one teacher before moving to another.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r2.anchor: والسبب الموجب لعدم تعرض المتقدمين إليه هو عظم هممهم، وكثرة حرصهم، ومبالغتهم في الإكثار من هذا العلم واستيعاب رواياته

NASHR:v2p194#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن علي بن عبد الغني الحصري القيرواني
NASHR:v2p194#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥuṣrī read the seven readings to Abū Bakr al-Qaṣrī in ninety completions, beginning at age ten and finishing over ten years, as his poem states.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r3.anchor: ولقد قرأ الأستاذ أبو الحسن علي بن عبد الغني الحصري القيرواني القراءات السبع على شيخه أبي بكر القصري تسعين ختمة

NASHR:v2p194#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r4.speaker: أبو حفص الكتاني
NASHR:v2p194#2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥafṣ al-Kattānī reports that although he stayed with Ibn Mujāhid for years reading only ʿĀṣim, Ibn Mujāhid refused his request to transfer to another reading.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r4.anchor: وكان أبو حفص الكتاني من أصحاب ابن مجاهد وممن لازمه كثيرا وعرف به، وقرأ عليه سنين لا يتجاوز قراءة عاصم

NASHR:v2p194#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r5.speaker: أبو الفتح فرج بن عمر الواسطي
NASHR:v2p194#2/r5.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ Faraj ibn ʿUmar al-Wāsiṭī read several completions in Abū Bakr's narration through Yaḥyā al-ʿAlīmī to Ibn al-Shaʿīr over several years.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو الفتح فرج بن عمر الواسطي أحد شيوخ ابن سوار القرآن برواية أبي بكر من طريق يحيى العليمي

NASHR:v2p194#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p194#2/r6.claim: Through the first half of the fifth century, the established practice was a separate full completion for each narration, not combining narrations; later, combining readings within one completion emerged and continued.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r6.anchor: وهذا الذي كان عليه الصدر الأول، ومن بعدهم إلى أثناء المائة الخامسة عصر الداني وابن شيطا الأهوازي والهذلي، ومن بعدهم فمن ذلك الوقت ظهر جمع القراءات في الختمة الواحدة

NASHR:v2p194#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p194#2/r7.speaker: بعض الأئمة
NASHR:v2p194#2/r7.claim: Some imams disliked combining readings in one completion because it was not the early generations' custom, but the author says this practice eventually became settled, accepted, and followed.
NASHR:v2p194#2/r7.anchor: وكان بعض الأئمة يكره ذلك من حيث إنه لم تكن عادة السلف عليه ولكن الذي استقر عليه العمل هو الأخذ به والتقرير عليه وتلقيه بالقبول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r1.claim: “Humbled” is circumstantial to those summoned; their eyes are the grammatical subject because humility’s effect appears in them.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r1.anchor: حال من مرفوع يدعون على أن أبصارهم مرتفع به على الفاعلية ونسبة الخشوع إلى الأبصار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r2.claim: Humility is attributed to the eyes because its visible effect appears there.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r2.anchor: ونسبة الخشوع إلى الأبصار لظهور أثره فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r3.claim: “Overtake them” means that humiliation reaches and covers them.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r5.claim: They had been summoned to prostrate in worldly life; stating the summons explicitly instead of using a pronoun adds emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r5.anchor: في الدنيا والإظهار في موضع الإضمار لزيادة التقرير

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r6.speaker: النخعي والشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r6.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī and al-Shaʿbī take prostration here as the prescribed prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r6.anchor: أو لأن المراد به الصلوات المكتوبة كما قال النخعي والشعبي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r7.claim: Another view takes prostration to mean all acts of obedience, with the summons being the summons of religious obligation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r7.anchor: أو جميع الطاعات كما قيل والدعوة دعوة التكليف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jubayr say they heard the call to prayer but did not answer it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن جبير كانوا يسمعون الأذان والنداء للصلاة فلا يجيبون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r9.claim: They were fully able to prostrate, yet refused to respond to the summons.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r9.anchor: متمكنون منه أقوى تمكن أي فلا يجيبون إليه ويأبونه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p36#2/r10.claim: The statement that they did not answer is omitted because it is obvious from context.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r1.claim: Believers lift their heads from prostration with faces whiter than snow, while disbelievers' and hypocrites' faces turn black.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r1.anchor: المؤمنين يرفعون رءوسهم من السجود ووجوههم أشد بياضا من الثلج وتسود وجوه الكافرين والمنافقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r2.claim: The humiliation that overwhelms them is the disgrace of regret and remorse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r2.anchor: ترهقهم ذلة} يغشاهم ذل الندامة والحسرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the call to prostrate means the prescribed prayer announced by the adhan and iqama.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r3.anchor: قال إبراهيم التيمي: يعني إلى الصلاة المكتوبة بالأذان والإقامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says they heard the call Hayya ʿala al-falah but did not answer it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا يسمعون حي على الفلاح فلا يجيبون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r5.claim: They were physically healthy and able, yet did not come to prostrate.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says the verse was revealed specifically about people who stay away from congregational prayers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p200/r6.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا عن الذين يتخلفون عن الجماعات.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r1.claim: Humiliation overtakes them while their eyes are downcast.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r2.claim: They had been called to prostrate in worldly life or while they were healthy.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:43-47/r3.claim: In life they had the ability to prostrate and were free of impediments.

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r1.claim: A report transmitted by al-Ṭabarī from Ibn Masʿūd through Abū al-Zaʿrāʾ says God appears and asks whom people worship; believers recognize and prostrate, while hypocrites’ backs become rigid and joined.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r1.anchor: فيقول: هل تعرفون ربكم؟ فيقولون: سبحانه إذا اعترف إلينا

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also cites an Ibn Masʿūd report saying the Merciful uncovers His shin; believers prostrate and hypocrites’ backs become one rigid surface.

BINTSHATI:v2p68/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r9.claim: The Day of Judgment is an appalling hardship for disbelievers: they are called to prostrate as a belated rebuke after wasting their worldly chance, when they were safe and able.
BINTSHATI:v2p68/r9.anchor: وأي شدة أفظع هولاً على الكافرين من يوم الحساب، حين يدعون إلى السجود تعجيزاً وتحسيراً وتقريعاً قد فاتت

BINTSHATI:v2p69/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r1.claim: Physical explanations say the backbones lose their joints, the vertebrae fuse into one, or the body becomes rigid after a forty-year wait and a divine manifestation; the author rejects such elaborations as incompatible with the text and context.
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r1.anchor: فذلك، ومثله كثير، مما لا يحتمله منهجنا في الأخذ بنص الآيات البينات، لفظاً وسياقاً

BINTSHATI:v2p69/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r2.claim: The inability to prostrate means the time for worship and the period of religious obligation have passed, rather than a bodily disability.
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r2.anchor: والأولى أن يحمل العجز عن السجود على فوات أوان التعبد ومهلة التكليف

BINTSHATI:v2p69/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r3.claim: The missed opportunity parallels al-Fajr’s scene of Hell brought forth and the sinner’s belated wish that he had prepared for his true life, after rejecting responsibility and loving wealth.
BINTSHATI:v2p69/r3.anchor: ونظيره ما في آيات الفجر، في سياق الحديث عن مصير الطغاة والمفسدين في الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r9.claim: Khāshiʿah means humble and submissive; the eyes disclose what is in the heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r9.anchor: لأن ما في القلب يعرف في العين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r10.claim: Believers will raise faces brighter than the sun, while the faces of disbelievers and hypocrites will be black and dark.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r10.anchor: أن المؤمنين يرفعون رؤوسهم ووجوههم أضوأ من الشمس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r11.claim: Tarhaquhum means shame covers and overpowers them, a great humiliation caused by using God-given limbs for pleasures that distance them from Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r11.anchor: لأنهم استعملوا الأعضاء التي أعطاهموها سبحانه وتعالى ليتقربوا بها إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r12.claim: They had been called to prostrate in earthly life by callers to God but refused, though physically able; arrogance, not bodily weakness, held them back.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r12.anchor: في الدنيا من كل داع يدعو إلينا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r13.claim: Sālimūn means physically sound and able, with no bodily impediment to prostration.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.claim: The passage uses iḥtibāk: inability in the first verse implies omitted ability in the second, while safety in the second implies omitted unsafety in the first.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p112/r14.anchor: ذكر عدم الاستطاعة أولا دال على حذف الاستطاعة ثانيا

DURR-FULL:v8p254/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the unbelievers were invited to prostrate safely in worldly life but are now summoned in fear; God kept the polytheists from obedience in both lives, linking worldly failure to inability to hear or see.
DURR-FULL:v8p254/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون} قال: هم الكفار كانوا يدعون

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas describes the lifting of the veil: believers who trusted God prostrate, while those who did not believe cannot; they had been able to prostrate safely in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r3.anchor: عن الغطاء فيقع من كان آمن به في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.claim: Qatāda calls the unveiling a horrendous, momentous affair and reports that believers prostrate while hypocrites' backs stiffen; their prostration brings hypocrites humiliation and regret.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {يوم يكشف عن ساق} قال: أمر فظيع جليل {ويدعون إلى السجود فلا يستطيعون} قال: ذلكم يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r5.claim: Qatāda explains the former invitation to prostrate as the calls to the prescribed prayers.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r5.anchor: وفي قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون} قال: في الصلوات

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.speaker: كعب الحبر
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears that the verses were revealed about the five obligatory prayers when they are called.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r6.anchor: عن كعب الحبر قال: والذي أنزل التوراة على موسى والإنجيل على عيسى والزبور على داود

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the invitation to prostrate means the congregational prayers.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود} قال: الصلوات في الجماعات

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the invitation as a man hearing the call to prayer but not answering it.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود} قال: الرجل يسمع الأذان فلا يجيب الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan transmits a Prophetic scene in which idol-worshippers follow their objects, Jews and Christians are turned away, and Muslims remain to be tested before being permitted to prostrate.
DURR-FULL:v8p256/r9.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يجمع الله الخلائق يوم القيامة ثم ينادي مناد

DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.claim: In al-Ḥasan's report, Christians are also turned away, Muslims recognize God by a sign, and believers prostrate while hypocrites cannot; Ibn Masʿūd's Prophetic report adds that each person's light varies with deeds and may flicker at the feet.
DURR-FULL:v8p257/r1.anchor: لهم: لستم من موسى وليس موسى منكم فيصرف بهم ذات الشمال ثم يقال للنصارى: ما كنتم تعبدون

DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's report says Muslims affirm worshipping God alone; believers fall prostrate when the ساق is unveiled, but hypocrites' backs remain rigid, fulfilling the warning that they had been invited while safe.
DURR-FULL:v8p259/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه ذكر عنده الدجال فقال: يفترق ثلاث فرق تتبعه فرقة تتبعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.claim: The unstated group alludes to hypocrites raised among Muslims: the prostration test honors true believers and exposes hypocrites who cannot bow.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p97/r8.anchor: فالوجه أن يكون عائدا إلى غير مذكور ، أي ويدعى مدعوون فيكون تعريضا بالمنافقين بأنهم يحشرون مع المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r8.claim: “Humbled” describes eyes looking down in abasement and fear, borrowed from a subdued person’s posture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r8.anchor: وخشوع الأبصار : هيئة النظر بالعين بذلة وخوف ، استعير له وصف { خاشعة } لأن الخاشع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r9.claim: Tarhaquhum means humiliation descends on and approaches them eagerly, intent on overtaking them; compare 80:41.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r9.anchor: و { ترهقهم } : تحل بهم وتقترب منهم بحرص على التمكن منهم ، رهق من باب فرح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r10.claim: “Humiliation overwhelms them” is a second circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in “they are unable.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r10.anchor: وجملة { ترهقهم ذلة } حال ثانية من ضمير { يستطيعون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r11.claim: The parenthetic clause recalls that in worldly life they were called to worship God alone while sound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r11.anchor: معترضة بين ما قبلها وما تفرع عنها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r12.claim: The waw marks a circumstantial clause: in worldly life they were physically able, with no bodily ailment preventing prostration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r12.anchor: والواو للحال وللاعتراض . وجملة { وهم سالمون } حال من ضمير { يدعون } أي وهم قادرون لا علة تعوقهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r13.claim: Salāma means absence of defects and diseases, unlike their compelled inability to prostrate at the Resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p99/r13.anchor: والسلامة : انتفاء العلل والأمراض بخلاف حالهم يوم القيامة فإنهم ملجأون لعدم السجود .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r17.claim: خاشعة is an accusative circumstantial expression describing their state.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r18.claim: All their limbs are humbled; eyes are singled out because their humility is clearest there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r18.anchor: وجوارحهم كلها خاشعة، أي ذليلة ولكنه خص الأبصار بالذكر لأن الخشوع فيها أبين منه في كل جارحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r19.claim: The humiliation overwhelms their souls and appears on them in a way that disgraces them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r19.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ترهقهم ذلة أي تزعج نفوسهم وتظهر عليهم ظهورا يخزيهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r20.claim: They had been called to prostrate in worldly life, when their backs were still free of the rigidity that now joins their vertebrae.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r20.anchor: يريد في دار الدنيا وهم سالمون مما نال عظام ظهورهم من الاتصال والعتو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r21.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r21.claim: Some interpreters take prostration as a figure for all acts of obedience, singling it out as the greatest act and the test in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r21.anchor: وقال بعض المتأولين: «السجود» هنا عبارة عن جميع الطاعات، وخص «السجود» بالذكر من حيث هو عظم الطاعات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r22.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي والشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r22.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi and al-Shaʿbi identify prostration here with the obligatory prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r22.anchor: وقال إبراهيم التيمي والشعبي: أراد ب السجود الصلوات المكتوبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r23.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r23.claim: Ibn Jubayr explains the call as hearing the prayer summons Hayya ʿala al-falah and failing to answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r23.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: المعنى كانوا يسمعون النداء للصلاة: وحي على الفلاح فلا يجيبون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r24.speaker: فلج الربيع بن خثيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r24.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym, despite needing support between two men to reach the mosque, said anyone hearing the call to success must answer, even crawling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r24.anchor: وفلج الربيع بن خيثم: فكان يهادي بين رجلين إلى المسجد، فقيل له: إنك لمعذور، فقال: من سمع حي على الفلاح، فليجب ولو حبوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r25.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r25.speaker: ابن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r25.claim: When warned that Tariq meant to kill him and urged to stay home, Ibn al-Musayyib refused to ignore the call to success.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p352/r25.anchor: وقيل لابن المسيب: إن طارقا يريد قتلك فاجلس في بيتك، فقال: أسمع حي على الفلاح فلا أجيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r1.claim: Their eyes are lowered and submissive.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r3.claim: In worldly life they were called to prayer by the adhān and ordered to perform the obligatory prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r3.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود يعني بالأذان في دار الدنيا ويؤمرون بالصلاة المكتوبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r4.claim: They were healthy and had no iron spits in their backs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r4.anchor: وهم سالمون أي معافون ليس في أصلابهم مثل سفافيد الحديد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r5.speaker: كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r5.claim: Kaʿb swore that this verse was revealed specifically about those who stay away from congregational prayers; Ibn al-Jawzī calls it a warning for those who abandon congregational prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p342/r5.anchor: وفي هذا وعيد لمن ترك صلاة الجماعة وكان كعب يقول والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا في الذين يتخلفون عن الجماعات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r2.claim: Their eyes are humbled and humiliation overwhelms them in the Hereafter because of their worldly crimes and arrogance: they are punished with the opposite of their former state.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r2.anchor: وقوله: {خاشعة أبصارهم ترهقهم ذلة} أي: في الدار الآخرة بإجرامهم وتكبرهم في الدنيا، فعوقبوا بنقيض ما كانوا عليه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r3.claim: Those who refused prostration while healthy in worldly life will be unable to prostrate when the Lord manifests; believers prostrate, but disbelievers and hypocrites cannot, and attempts make them fall backward with flattened backs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p199/r3.anchor: ولما دعوا إلى السجود في الدنيا فامتنعوا منه مع صحتهم وسلامتهم كذلك عوقبوا بعدم قدرتهم عليه في الآخرة

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r12.claim: Their eyes are fearful and expectant of punishment; the eye is mentioned because its condition visibly displays the inner state.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r12.anchor: (خاشعة أبصارهم) أي: خائفة متوقعة للعذاب، وذكر العين؛ لأنه يظهر عليه أثره

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r13.claim: Humiliation overtakes them until their abasement and submissiveness become visible.
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r13.anchor: ترهقهم ذلة أي: تلحقهم ذلة حتى يتبين الخشوع والذلة عليهم

JISHUMI:v10p7041/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r14.claim: When healthy they could prostrate but refused; reports say they ignored obligatory prayers called by adhān and iqāma (Ibrāhīm al-Taymī and Saʿīd b. Jubayr), or skipped congregational prayers (Kaʿb).
JISHUMI:v10p7041/r14.anchor: وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود وهم سالمون أصحاء يمكنهم السجود فلا يسجدون، قيل: يدعون إلى السجود إلى الصلاة المكتوبة بالأذان والإقامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r13.claim: Ibn Masud explains that their backbones become one bone without joints, so they cannot bend when rising or lowering themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r13.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : تعقم أصلابهم واحدا ، أي ترد عظاما بلا مفاصل لا تنثني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r14.claim: A hadith says their spines remain one rigid piece, meaning a single vertebra.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r14.anchor: وفي الحديث : وتبقى أصلابهم طبقا واحدا ، أي ، فقارة واحدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r15.claim: They are summoned to prostrate as rebuke, not legal worship; fused backs prevent them, increasing regret for refusing when sound and able in life.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p598/r15.anchor: لا يدعون إليه تعبدا وتكليفا ، ولكن توبيخا وتعنيفا على تركهم السجود في الدنيا

MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports the Prophet saying that those who prostrated willingly in life will be allowed to prostrate, while those who did so from fear or ostentation will be unable, their backs made rigid so they fall on them.
MUJAHID:v2p689#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول يكشف ربنا عز وجل عن ساقه

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r5.claim: Their eyes are lowered when they see the Fire.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r5.anchor: { خاشعة أبصارهم } عند معاينة النار { ترهقهم ذلة }

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r6.claim: The phrase means humiliation overwhelms and covers them.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r6.anchor: { ترهقهم ذلة } يعني تشغاهم مذلة { وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود }

MUQATIL:68:42-43/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r7.claim: They had been commanded to perform the five prayers while healthy and safe in worldly life; their backs then become like iron spits.
MUQATIL:68:42-43/r7.anchor: { وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود } يعني يؤمرون بالصلوات الخمس { وهم سالمون } [آية: 43] يقول: كانوا معافون في الدينا

MUQATIL:70:8-18/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r5.claim: Muqatil links the lowered, humiliated eyes at sight of the Fire to the description in al-Qalam.
MUQATIL:70:8-18/r5.anchor: خاشعة أبصارهم [القلم: 43] خافضة أبصارهم ذليلة عند معاينة النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r1.claim: “خاشعة” is a circumstantial accusative referring to the pronoun in “يدعون”: they are summoned while their eyes are humbled.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r1.anchor: ذليلة حال من الضمير في يدعون ﴿ أبصارهم ﴾ أي يدعون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r2.anchor: ﴿ ترهقهم ذلة ﴾ يغشاهم صغار ﴿ وقد كانوا يدعون ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r3.claim: Prophets called them to prostrate in worldly life while they were healthy, but they refused; that refusal is why they are barred later.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p272/r3.anchor: في الدنيا ﴿ وهم سالمون ﴾ أي وهم اصحاء فلا يسجدون

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.claim: One explanation describes a dying, weakened patient uncovering his shin; the caller summons him to prayer, but he cannot rise and go out.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43/r12.anchor: وقيل: يريد وقت اقتراب الأجل وضعف البدن أي يكشف المريض عن ساقه ليبصر ضعفه، ويدعوه المؤذن إلى الصلاة فلا يمكنه أن يقوم ويخرج.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports that on Judgment Day each people follows what it worshipped; the monotheists await their Lord, recognize Him despite not having seen Him, and prostrate when the veil is lifted, while some cannot. The account ends with each being replaced by a Jew or Christian in Hell; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو الليث السمرقندي في تفسيره: حدثنا الخليل بن أحمد قال حدثنا ابن منيع قال حدثنا هدبة قال حدثنا حماد بن سلمة عن علي بن زيد عن عمارة القرشي عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى قال حدثني أبي قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.claim: Abu Bardah swore three times that his father had told him the Abu Musa report; Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said he had heard no report about monotheists he liked more.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو بردة: فحدثت بهذا الحديث عمر بن عبد العزيز فقال: الله الذي لا إله إلا هو لقد حدثك أبوك بهذا الحديث؟

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.claim: Qays ibn al-Sakan reports Ibn Masud's account: after a forty-year standing and a call about divine justice, groups follow their objects of worship into Hell; Muslims and hypocrites await God, but sincere worshippers prostrate when He is revealed and hypocrites cannot.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r2.anchor: وقال قيس بن السكن: حدث عبد الله بن مسعود عند عمر بن الخطاب فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.claim: Qurtubi says the meaning of the Abu Musa and Ibn Masud accounts is established in Sahih Muslim through Abu Said al-Khudri and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r3.anchor: قلت: معنى حديث أبي موسى وابن مسعود ثابت في صحيح مسلم من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري وغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r4.claim: Their eyes are humbled and abased.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r5.claim: Khāshiʿatan is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r6.claim: Believers lift their heads with faces whiter than snow, while hypocrites' and disbelievers' faces blacken beyond pitch.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r6.anchor: وذلك أن المؤمنين يرفعون رؤوسهم ووجوههم أشد بياضا من الثلج.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r7.claim: The call to prostrate was made in worldly life, when they were sound and healthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وقد كانوا يدعون إلى السجود } أي في الدنيا. { وهم سالمون } معافون أصحاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r8.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi explains that they were called through the adhan and iqama but refused.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r8.anchor: قال إبراهيم التيمي: أي يدعون بالأذان والإقامة فيأبونه.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r9.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says they heard 'come to success' but did not answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا يسمعون حي على الفلاح فلا يجيبون.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r10.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r10.claim: Kaab al-Ahbar says the verse was revealed specifically about those who stay away from congregational prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r10.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والله ما نزلت هذه الآية إلا في الذين يتخلفون عن الجماعات.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r11.claim: Another explanation takes the call as the religious obligation imposed on them; Qurtubi says the explanations are close and refers to his earlier discussion of congregational prayer's obligation in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r11.anchor: وقيل: أي بالتكليف الموجه عليهم في الشرع والمعنى متقارب. وقد مضى في سورة «البقرة» الكلام في وجوب صلاة الجماعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r12.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r12.claim: Though paralyzed, al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym was carried between two men to the mosque; when offered the home-prayer concession, he said anyone hearing the call should answer, even crawling.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r12.anchor: وكان الربيع بن خيثم قد فلج وكان يهادي بين الرجلين إلى المسجد فقيل: يا أبا يزيد، لو صليت في بيتك

QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r13.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r13.claim: When Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib was urged to hide from Tariq, who sought to kill him, he asked whether he could hide from God; told to remain home, he insisted that he heard 'come to success' and must answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:42-43#3/r13.anchor: وقيل لسعيد بن المسيب: إن طارقا يريد قتلك فتغيب.
